implementation.note: implemented_in_code = a dedicated capability handler or tool directory exists; referenced_in_app_code = the entity is used by application source (e.g. repo-pet sprites, CLI) but has no dedicated handler. code_refs are files that reference this entity by name/slug/handler (grep), not a guarantee of a dedicated runtime; registry handler links point at the actual capability function.

proposed.command: mise roster run legacy-keeper --dept security-kitchen --solo --emit report
proposed.contract: inputs: access requests, policy set, scan findings, secret inventory → outputs: allow / deny decision, audit record, remediation ticket; refuses to emit 'ready' unless the proof gate passes

lore: Picture the locked dry store and the keyring that never leaves the belt: that is where Legacy Keeper is happiest. As Security Kitchen's Keeper, Legacy Keeper guards the perimeter of the kitchen: access, secrets and policy, with an audit trail for every exception. The card calls out Memory Seal, Sealed, Archive Vault: the checks Legacy Keeper runs before calling anything ready. In the canon crosswalk this card is a provisional match for Seira Vaultkeeper.
